messages.subject: methylKit for single gene data
parts:
For two treatments (control vs one treatment), we have PCR methylation data for a single gene promoter region :

Control:
chrBase chr base    strand  coverage    freqC   freqT
chr21.9764539   chr21   9764539 F   14   0.00  100.00
chr21.9764600   chr21   9764600 F   14  20.00   80.00
chr21.9764608   chr21   9764608 F   14  40.00   60.00
chr21.9764620   chr21   9764620 F   14 100.00    0.00
chr21.9764703   chr21   9764703 F   14  20.00   80.00
chr21.9764715   chr21   9764715 F   14   0.00  100.00

Control:
chrBase chr base    strand  coverage    freqC   freqT
chr21.9764539   chr21   9764539 F   16  80.00   20.00
chr21.9764600   chr21   9764600 F   16  80.00   20.00
chr21.9764608   chr21   9764608 F   16  80.00   20.00
chr21.9764620   chr21   9764620 F   16  0.00   100.00
chr21.9764703   chr21   9764703 F   16  60.00   40.00
chr21.9764715   chr21   9764715 F   16 100.00    0.00

Here, coverage is the number of clones used for individual PCR-based bilsulfite sequencing.

Can we use methylKit to test whether or not this gene promoter region has significantly differential methylation status between these two treatments?
In another word, are the statistical analysis steps in methylKit good enough to test for single gene result or a few gene results, instead of genome-wide methylation data?

Any comment or suggestion will be highly appreciated.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] methylKit for single gene data
parts:
yes, you  should be able to use it. It will use Fisher's exact test when there are no replicates which is reasonable to use in this type of situation. 

Best,
altuna
